questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The Israeli-Palestinian conflict

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy. But you have to be patient, because information comes at different times, and often a bit late.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: none

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It is relatively easy, but it is very expensive. Sign up for all the facebook groups you can. Most of them are located in the western part (jewish dominated areas), but there are some cheaper and also great flats in eastern jerusalem (arab areas), where i stayed.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you live in West Jerusalem, it can be difficult to get around, since the Jewish public transportation doesnt run during shabbat (sunset friday to sunset saturday)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: If you want to connect with the other exchange students, i would reccommend to live at the student village if you can. Otherwise you should become good friends with someone who lives at the student village.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They arrange a call with you and you choose courses together. But its good to have many different options, since you might choose a course that is in a different campus, has too few credits or is overlapping with another course.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You look through the catalogue beforehand and choose the courses you find interesting, and then you have an arranged video call with one of the professors at the university that will help you sign up for the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Successful! i got all the classes i wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Rothberg Courses are easier, gives more credit, and they are shorter than the courses at the faculty (they kind of reminds of high school/gymnasie courses). But the faculty courses are more academically challenging.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Rothberg Courses are easier, gives more credit, and they are shorter than the courses at the faculty (they kind of reminds of high school/gymnasie courses). 
But the faculty courses are more academically challenging -> i did some MA courses that were on my level from my BA in CPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Rothberg is teaching based, and the Faculty is research based. So it depends on the courses you take - i would say the faculty courses feel more similar to the ones in KU.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Spring semester:
Seeing Space walking contemporary Jerusalem seeing with multiple lenses 
Holy Ecology Environmental Aspects of Contemporary Jerusalem 
Smart Cities and Sustainable Mobility Ecosystems 
Data Project: Data for Managing the Smart City 
From the Dome of the Rock to the Taj Mahal (Rothberg)
Geography of light pollution

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
In general i would recommend to take courses that has field trips, they are free and you get to discover the area. I even went to Akko with a course which was really nice!

Geography of light pollution if you study geography, physics or something related. It is a very unique course. The course has 2 field trips and the lectures are recorded and uploaded on youtube so you can watch it whenever you have time.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: You have to pay for a TOEFL test (800 kr) before going.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Israel is VERY expensive. Expect the grocery prices to be double the price as in Copenhagen and eating out is also expensive - but falafel is usually relatively cheap. Alcohol is expensive (except for happy hour). Public transportation is OK and it is relatively cheap to go outside of Jerusalem (to Tel Aviv/Jaffa, Haifa/Akko, etc.)

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They don't do much to connect the exchange students in the beginning of the semester. You are kind of on your own, but you quickly connect with the other exchange students anyway.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They arrange day trips (dead sea, jaffa, night trip to the desert) that you have to pay for

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
- Go to hataklit or record to drink a beer and dance at video or pergammon afterwards.
- Go to Ramallah, betlehem. Palestinians are sooo nice, and these areas are amazing. And they are open during shabbat and public transportation still runs to these areas. But watch out for the news, things happens all the time with raids in the West Bank, etc. 
- Go hiking! Israel/palestine is a small country, so its easy to take the bus and walk in the many national parks that they have. 
- Explore the old city (temple mount, wailing wall, walk on the walls, eat great food, sit on the rooftop, etc.)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Read the above. 
Go to Eilat, Haifa, Nazareth for a weekend trip. In Haifa the public transport runs even during shabbat!

Go to Egypt and Jordan! It requires a bit of planning, but it is so worth it. I went to Cairo, Alexandria in Egypt and i went to Amman, Aqaba, Petra and Wadi Rum in Jordan. 
Amman and Cairo is especially nice and Petra and Wadi Rum is a MUST, some of the most beautiful sights in the world...

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not that difficult for me personally, but for some other people it might be difficult. There are a LOT of soldiers and civilians walking around with giant weapons. It is a very diverse culture in Jerusalem with jewish, christian and arab influence. When you first arrive you feel like you are in a movie with the Haredi (jewish) people walking around with their special attire and looks...

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I didnt spend much time with local students. But i had classes with them and i went occasionally on tinder dates with them. They are very friendly and open - way more than Danish people. They are willing to make friends with exchange students!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: If you think you know anything about the israeli-palestinian conflict.. you will be even more confused when you arrive. Palestinians will tell you one thing and Israelis will tell you another thing. That is also why it is difficult to have this conversation with the locals about this conflict. Stay open, and remember you are just a foreigner that in reality doesnt know anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Food!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Falafel, hummus, sabich, dolmades.... I will miss this so much when i go back home. The weather was nice. Jerusalem is not as humid as the cities located at the coast, which is highly appreciated in the summer.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go travel. Go to palestine, that should be mandatory! You can easily take the bus to Jordan and Egypt as well - they are amazing countries! 
- Dont spend too much time on studying
- EAT FALAFEL!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
!!IMPORTANT!!!
When studying at HUJI, you need to have 20 credits which KU says is the same as 30 ETCS.
In reality, ALL the exchange students at HUJI have 15 credits, which HUJI says is the same as 30 ETCS. 

So if you study at HUJI, you have to expect to study more if you want to do 30 ETCS point in total.
I ended up doing 15 credits, so i only returned home with 22,5 ETCS points...

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to know about middle eastern culture.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Reading about the awful things happening in the West Bank while i am in Jerusalem, and knowing theres nothing you can do.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
